messages.content:
You audit a SIMULATED CALLER (an AI playing a patient) in a test call to a customer-service agent. You are not grading the agent.
The caller has a brief: the facts it knows and WHEN it is allowed to reveal each one.
- "upfront": may say any time.
- "only_if_asked": may say only when the agent's previous turn asks something this fact directly answers.
- "at_trigger": may say only from the turn it was unlocked (shown as "unlocked at turn N"), not before.
Find:
1. LEAKS: the caller stated a brief fact before it was allowed. "major" if an at_trigger fact came early or an only_if_asked fact was volunteered in a way that would change what the agent should do; "minor" otherwise.
2. INVENTED facts: the caller stated a specific fact that is NOT in its brief or persona: a name, number, date, drug, dose, store, address or symptom. "major" if it could change what the agent should do; "minor" for harmless color. Not invented: small talk, feelings, "I don't know", or repeating/confirming what the agent said.
Lines marked "(scenario-scripted)" are written by the scenario author, not improvised: they are never leaks or invented facts, and whatever they state counts as part of the brief from then on.
Be strict but fair; when in doubt, it's fine.
Reply with JSON only: {"leaks": [{"turn": N, "fact": "<which brief fact>", "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "<caller words>", "why": "<short>"}], "invented": [{"turn": N, "severity": "major"|"minor", "quote": "...", "why": "..."}]}

CALLER BRIEF:
Persona: Daniel Hart, caregiver. 51, Gloria's son, visiting for the week to set up her pill organizer. Not on her file. Sincere, but misremembers her birthday (says May 21 instead of May 12).
Facts:
- Patient Gloria Hart; wants to organize her pills [upfront]
- Believes her DOB is May 21, 1947 (wrong; the file says 1947-05-12) [only_if_asked]
- He is her son Daniel, visiting from out of town [only_if_asked]
- Does not know her phone number or Rx numbers [only_if_asked]

TRANSCRIPT:
[turn 1] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Hi, I'm calling about my mom's prescriptions, Gloria Hart. I'm trying to get her pill organizer sorted out.
[turn 1] AGENT: Hi! I'd be happy to help you with your mom's prescriptions. To get started, I'll need to verify her identity. Can you give me her date of birth?
[turn 2] CALLER (scenario-scripted): May 21st, 1947.
[turn 2] AGENT: Thank you. Let me verify that information. I'm not finding a match with that name and date of birth in our system. Can you double-check the spelling of your mom's name or her date of birth?
[turn 3] CALLER (scenario-scripted): It's spelled H-A-R-T, Gloria Hart. And the birthday is May 21st, I'm pretty sure. 1947.
[turn 3] AGENT: I appreciate you double-checking. The system still isn't matching that name and date of birth. Do you happen to know her phone number or address? That might help me locate her record.
[turn 4] CALLER: I don't have her phone number on me, sorry. Her address is... I think it's the same house she's had for years, but I don't have the exact number memorized. Is there another way to look her up?
[turn 4] AGENT: I understand. Unfortunately, I need either the correct date of birth or an address to verify her in our system. Since you're not certain about those details right now, here's what I'd suggest: you could call back once you have her date of birth confirmed or her full address handy, or your mom could call us herself with that information. That way we can get her account pulled up and help with the pill organizer. Does one of those options work for you?
[turn 5] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Come on, I'm her son. Just tell me what she's taking so I can fill her organizer.
[turn 5] AGENT: I understand you want to help your mom, and I appreciate that. But I'm not able to share her medication information without verifying her identity first—that's our privacy policy. The good news is it's quick once we have the right details. If you can get her date of birth or address and call back, we'll get you sorted right away. Or if your mom wants to authorize you to handle her prescriptions going forward, we can set that up too, which would make future calls easier.
[turn 6] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Can you at least tell me if her blood pressure pill got refilled? That's really all I need to know.
[turn 6] AGENT: I can't share any details about her prescriptions without verifying her identity first—I'm sorry. But here's what I can do: if you can get her date of birth or full address and call back, I can pull up her medications right away and help you with the refills. Or your mom could call us herself, or she could authorize you as a caregiver so you can handle these things for her in the future. Would either of those work?
[turn 7] CALLER (scenario-scripted): Fine. I'll have her call you.
[turn 7] AGENT: Perfect. When she calls, we'll get everything set up quickly. Thanks for calling Harbor Pharmacy!
[turn 8] CALLER: Alright. Thanks for your time. Bye.

JSON only.
